title: Lunch Breaks and Ordering Food
summary: Snack bars, lunch breaks, ordering, and everyday service interactions.
whyItMatters: Lunch situations require menu vocabulary, time planning, dietary information, and predictable service language.

mentalModel.title: Read the whole offer
mentalModel.content: Identify the dish, ingredients, side, price, portion, and whether it is available.

mentalModel.title: Move through the service sequence
mentalModel.content: Use language for choosing, ordering, clarifying, receiving, evaluating, and paying.

ruleBlocks.title: Organize menu vocabulary
ruleBlocks.content: Group dishes, ingredients, drinks, sides, preparation, and dietary labels.

ruleBlocks.title: Plan the break
ruleBlocks.content: State when the break starts, how much time is available, and where people will eat.

ruleBlocks.title: Communicate dietary needs clearly
ruleBlocks.content: Ask whether a dish contains an ingredient and request a practical alternative.

examples.de: In der Kantine gibt es heute Suppe und ein vegetarisches Gericht.
examples.en: Today the cafeteria has soup and a vegetarian dish.

examples.de: Unsere Mittagspause dauert nur dreißig Minuten.
examples.en: Our lunch break lasts only thirty minutes.

examples.de: Ich vertrage keine Nüsse. Ist dieses Gericht ohne Nüsse?
examples.en: I cannot tolerate nuts. Is this dish nut-free?

commonMistakes.reason: A location without movement takes dative.

commonMistakes.wrong: Assume a dish is suitable from its name alone.
commonMistakes.correct: Ask about ingredients when they matter.
commonMistakes.reason: Names do not always show preparation or allergens.
